# Myto

> Myto is a local-first AI coding workspace. It reads your project, uses the tools you approve, and helps carry work through implementation and verification.

## Primary pages

- Product page: /
- Download page: /download — the platform chooser; every "Download" control on the site leads here
- Chat: /chat — a live, model-backed chat for Myto, styled like a full chat app; ask a question and it streams an answer. Backed by a same-origin server gateway with a free per-visitor token budget.
- Discover: /discover — the community feed: text-only posts about AI, Myto, crypto and more, with link previews, reactions, comments, and follows. Public to read; Google/GitHub sign-in to write.
- Authentication: /authentication — Google/GitHub sign-in and the per-account bring-your-own-key model configuration the apps sync from.
- Machine-readable guide: /llms.txt

## Product facts

- Platform: Windows 10 and 11 (64-bit) and Android are supported today. A browser build is available at https://mytocode.vercel.app.
- Current release: v0.9.2 — a Windows installer (Myto-Setup.exe) and a native Android APK (myto.apk) ship together from GitHub Releases.
- Price: the app is free; the only cost is whatever model provider you choose to use.
- Privacy: Myto is local-first — it works from your project on your machine, with the integrations you configure.
- Models: a local Ollama endpoint (http://localhost:11434 by default) or any OpenAI-compatible endpoint configured in Settings. Reasoning effort is a per-turn setting from low to max.
- Core workflow: understand the repository, plan, use approved tools, edit, and verify the build.
- Approvals: reads run automatically, edits are shown as a diff before they are written, and commands, network access, and destructive steps ask first. Permission modes are ask-every-time, auto-approve-edits, and autonomous.
- Extensibility: Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers and Markdown Skills extend the workspace; slash commands and plugins are available in the chat.
- Also included: a real terminal, a live dev-server preview it can inspect, the Myto Browser, sub-agents with git-worktree isolation, background runs, MYTO.md project memory, hooks and scheduled tasks, image input, and a headless CLI (`myto -p "<prompt>"`, with `--json`).

## Page map

The product page is a single main landmark with labelled sections, in this order:

1. The hero — "Your coding agent, on any model." What Myto is in two lines and a Download call-to-action.
2. "Bring the model you choose" — the model families Myto runs, with the note that a local Ollama or any OpenAI-compatible endpoint works.
3. How it works — the four-step workflow: choose your model, describe the task, review each diff, ship it verified.
4. "A full coding workspace" (#features) — six capabilities, from multi-model support to verifying its own work.
5. Pricing (#pricing) — "$0. Free. You bring the model." with what is included.
6. Documentation (#docs) — "Up and running in a minute": a contents rail of tabbed topics (quick start, headless CLI, and more) that swaps the panel in place.

The download page (/download) is a separate document with its own heading, "Download Myto", then one block per platform under #platforms:

- Windows — Available now. Windows 10 or 11, 64-bit. Direct link to the Myto-Setup.exe installer. Self-signed, so SmartScreen warns on first run (More info → Run anyway).
- Android — Available now. Recent Android phones and tablets. Direct link to the myto.apk build. Self-signed, so Android asks you to allow the install the first time.
- iOS — Coming soon.

- Try in browser: https://mytocode.vercel.app

## Reading guidance

- All content is present in the initial document. Sections fade in on scroll, but that is a CSS opacity change only — nothing is loaded, injected, or gated behind it.
- Stable anchors on the product page: #top (hero), #features, #pricing, #docs. On /download: #platforms. On /discover: #feed. On /chat: the page has its own app-style sidebar instead of the site header and footer.
- The Download controls are supplementary; every page reads without operating them. Every one of them navigates to /download, except the direct installer and APK links on /download itself.
